submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent: 9.6e-7 A (Cu 0.50, Fe 0.17, V 0.33), close to the Cu3V2O8 Cu:V ratio. Models point the same way: FeVO4 is stable (MACE hull 0), but its HSE gap of 2.75 eV is above the 2.4 eV photons. Cu vanadate chemistry lowers the predicted gap (a hypothetical CuVO4 came out at about 1.15 eV), so Cu-rich films should absorb better.

rejected.reason: V-rich, measured 3.8e-7 A. Likely dominated by wide-gap V/FeVO4-type phases that absorb poorly at 2.4 eV.
Same Cu:V ratio with more Fe, measured 8.5e-7 A, slightly below 127. Adding Fe did not help.

consultations.verdict: Weak support: FeVO4 is on the hull (MACE) but its HSE gap 2.75 eV exceeds the 2.4 eV photons, so pure FeVO4 would absorb poorly. The Cu content in V-rich films should add Cu vanadate phases with smaller gaps, so this measurement checks the densely sampled V-rich region as a baseline.

Support: replacing Fe with Cu in the FeVO4 structure brings the predicted HSE gap down to about 1.15 eV. Films richer in Cu should therefore absorb 2.4 eV light much better than V-rich/FeVO4-like films. Measuring Cu-rich index 127 (Cu:V ~1.5, near Cu3V2O8, with some Fe) tests this. The structure is hypothetical, so this is a qualitative trend, not a value.

Mixed but supports staying Cu-rich. A Cu analog of the FeVO4 structure sits 0.112 eV/atom above the hull, so Cu should form its own Cu vanadates (e.g. Cu3V2O8) instead of entering the FeVO4 structure. Fe is likely present as a stable FeVO4-type co-phase or as an alloying element. Index 128 keeps the same Cu:V ratio as the best result so far (index 127, ~0.59) and adds a little Fe (0.22). This tests whether more Fe helps the Cu3V2O8-like phase.
